thread:
infra-alerts-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Sustained increase in OOM_KILL + CUDA_DRIVER_ERROR across r-serve-pool-6 (us-west-2). 15 nodes with repeated container restarts in last 20m. Pattern: paged-attention allocator memory growth (KV page fragmentation) -> slow creep to OOM. Auto-escalation to eng-oncall.

jamie_oncall: I'm on it. grabbing logs and starting handoff. pls ping if you see noise on console.

priyanka_sre: oncall handoff accepted. jamie, what metrics are you seeing?

jamie_oncall: 95th/99th latency spikes look aligned with GPU memory pressure events. Pod restarts = OOM_KILL in kernel logs. Allocator shows many small free segments -> fragmentation. Total used pages trending up even when qps flat.

ricardo_runtime: fyi we pushed the paged-attn allocator a month ago; it has a known slow-free code path that can fragment under certain KV churn. not sure if it's the same. can you paste a memory map?

jamie_oncall: pasting trimmed logs (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-15T15:12:03Z] pod/runtime-abc OOM_KILL: process 1234 (runner) total_vm: 3600000kB, anon_rss: 3200000kB
[2026-03-15T15:12:03Z] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 1234 (runner)
[2026-03-15T15:12:05Z] runtime: allocator: free_list len=2, small_fragments=312K, pages_in_use=2140, pages_freeable=40
[2026-03-15T15:12:05Z] runtime: kv_cache: entries=1.8M, avg_entry_pages=0.8, fragmented_pages=420
```

mike_engineer: run `kubectl exec` + `pmap` and `dmesg`? also `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` to confirm GPU OOM vs host OOM.

jamie_oncall: running commands now.

jamie_oncall: output: `nvidia-smi` shows <5% GPU memory free on several pods just before crash. dmesg shows both GPU driver messages and kernel oom_killer. So both sides stressed.

priyanka_sre: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) take affected pods out of rotation (drain), 2) increase eviction aggressiveness for paged cache (reducing TTL), 3) route heavy models to fallback small-variant images or Dedicated nodes if available. Thoughts?

ricardo_runtime: agree. Also we can toggle a runtime flag to force coalesced free (experimental) to reduce fragmentation — we have a hotfix branch that forces a synchronous free path that trades a bit of throughput for memory compaction. We can roll it to a subset of nodes.

jamie_oncall: action plan:
- step 1: drain 5 most-affected nodes in r-serve-pool-6 (manual) -> @oncall-bot will mark them maintenance.
- step 2: patch eviction TTL for kvcache from 600s -> 120s in config for r-serve-pool-6.
- step 3: deploy runtime hotfix to 3 nodes (canary) with compaction flag.
- step 4: rate-limit embedding-heavy routes by 30% for 30m.

oncall-bot: maintenance started on nodes: r-serve-pool-6-{a,b,c,d,e}. Pods draining.

natalie_support: Customer impact: support dashboard shows ~12 customers saw elevated 5xx between 15:05-15:40 UTC. Two enterprise customers (acme-corp, hallmark-data) reported intermittent failures. I sent short comms to both; sigma on priority.

ricardo_runtime: starting canary deploy of hotfix (branch: fix/alloc-compact-2026). Rolling to 3 nodes (r-serve-pool-6-canary-{1,2,3}). Will monitor retention and fragmentation metrics.

mike_engineer: command we used to increase eviction TTL: `kubectl patch cm runtime-config -n infra --type merge -p '{"data": {"kvcache.eviction_ttl": "120"}}'`

jamie_oncall: canary metrics: after hotfix live on canaries (10m): fragmented_pages dropped ~70% on canaries, pages_in_use stabilized. No new OOMs on canaries.

priyanka_sre: nice. continue canary for 20m, then expand to rest of pool. also keep evictions for 60m after stabilization.

ricardo_runtime: rolling hotfix to remaining r-serve-pool-6 nodes now (batch size 4). Patch note: forces immediate coalesce of small free runs when fragmentation threshold exceeded. Caveat: small perf hit on tail p99 CPU but avoids OOMs.

jamie_oncall: expanded patch rolled to all affected nodes. observed immediate drop in container restarts. No further OOM_KILL in last 17m.

natalie_support: updating customers: sent follow-up to impacted customers (inc. Acme) stating we mitigated allocator fragmentation causing memory creep, monitoring, and will follow up with RCA in postmortem.

priyanka_sre: customer impact summary for postmortem: ~12 customers affected, 2 enterprise had transient 5xx, total downtime window ~35m for worst-affected routes. No data loss. Need SLO blameless review.

jamie_oncall: root-cause hypothesis: under high KV churn workloads (embedding + long context chat), paged-attention allocator's lazy free path produced many sub-page free fragments that were not coalesced quickly -> fragmentation + slow memory leak -> host/GPU memory pressure -> OOM_KILL/CUDA driver errors.

ricardo_runtime: follow-ups from runtime team: implement deterministic compaction path, add fragmentation metrics (frag ratio histograms), add a fail-safe to reject new large-KV requests when frag ratio > 0.7, and add an autoscale target based on fragmented_pages.

mike_engineer: infra follow-ups: add alert that correlates paged-alloc fragmented_pages + OOM_KILL rate, add runbook step to increase eviction aggressiveness, and provide a script to bulk drain nodes.

priyanka_sre: I'll open an incident ticket and assign postmortem to ricardo + jamie. ETA for postmortem draft: EOD tomorrow.

oncall-bot: Incident acknowledged. Postmortem task created: PM-1799009999. Assigned: ricardo_runtime, jamie_oncall.

jamie_oncall: closing on-call thread for now; monitoring continues. ping if anything new. :white_check_mark:

natalie_support: adding support notes in internal status page with timeline and mitigation steps.

ricardo_runtime: created PR: #1428 with deterministic compaction, test harness included. will schedule perf run tomorrow.

priyanka_sre: thanks team. follow-up checklist:
- postmortem + timeline and customer comms
- new metrics & alerting
- allocator patch merged + perf verification
- runbook update (drain steps + config knobs)
- ensure Dedicated customers routed properly during future events

jamie_oncall: done for now.

natalie_support: marking incident as "mitigated" in support board.

oncall-bot: Incident mitigated at 2026-03-15T16:02:00Z.
